## Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Sole non-infrastructure host on the /24; source of all outbound C2 traffic |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (Intel) | Ethernet/ARP frames binding 172.17.0.99 to this MAC (`eth.src`/ARP replies) |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP Request option 12 (`4445534b544f502d524e564f394154`), NBNS `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>`, DNS queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| Domain | bepositive.com (AD domain, DC = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 at 172.17.0.17, MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd) | DHCP option 15, LDAP/Kerberos traffic to 172.17.0.17 |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (Andrew Fletcher) | Kerberos `CNameString=afletcher` on the AS/TGS exchange between 172.17.0.99↔172.17.0.17; LDAP bind referencing `CN=Andrew Fletcher,CN=Users,DC=bepositive,DC=com` |

### Malware family
**Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**. The provided Suricata/IDS alert export fires `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` directly on the 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197 POST traffic (Event #3.1504, 48 hits), corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser` on the same stream (Event #3.1497). Traffic behavior matches: periodic (~70–90s interval) `POST /foots.php` beacons with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` bodies to a bare IP (no hostname), each answered `200 text/html`, spanning from t=155s to the end of the capture (~3560s) — classic stealer C2 check-in cadence.

### Command-and-control / IOCs (all observed directly in the pcap)

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — evidence: 48× `POST /foots.php` beacons and 1× `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` + `POST /index.php`, all HTTP/1.1, User-Agent `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; …)` (spoofed legacy IE UA, no browser actually sends this). No DNS lookup precedes any of these connections — the malware connects to the IP directly, matching the "Dotted Quad" alert.

**URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeating C2 checkin/exfil POST endpoint (Koi Stealer signature match).
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — gate/registration request; response body (61 bytes, exported via `http.export`) is the pipe-delimited string `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, i.e. a bot-ID/sub-ID/C2-URL tuple — consistent with a loader/PPI-style install-confirmation gate that precedes stealer beaconing.
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — POST immediately following the GET above.

**Domain**
- None. 79.124.78.197 is contacted purely by IP; no A-record lookup for it appears anywhere in the DNS traffic. This is itself a grounded indicator (absence of DNS resolution for an active C2 IP).

**Files / hashes**
- No executable payload or attachment was transferred in this capture (HTTP object export yields only empty/near-empty bodies for `foots.php` — POST request bodies, not server-delivered files — and text artifacts like `connecttest.txt`, `ProcessMAU.txt`). No SHA256-hashable malware binary was observed in the traffic; infection predates the start of the capture (the host is already beaconing at t=155s with no prior download visible).

### Benign context (not IOCs)
- `172.17.0.17` / `win-ctl9xbq9y19.bepositive.com` — internal AD Domain Controller/DNS/DHCP server.
- `46.254.34.201` (TLS SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — an ordinary HTTPS connection, unrelated to the flagged alerts.
- Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update traffic: `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`, Bing/MSN endpoints, Akamai/Azure CDN IPs (23.x/20.x/13.x ranges) in the top-conversations list.
- SMB/NBNS/CLDAP/Kerberos chatter between 172.17.0.99 and 172.17.0.17 — normal AD domain-join/authentication behavior (the alert file's "SMBv1"/"NTLMSSP overflow"/"Kerberos overflow" signatures are generic heuristics on normal AD protocol traffic, not confirmed exploitation).

### Incident summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on the bepositive.com AD domain, was infected with **Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ETPRO Suricata rule). Starting at t≈155s the host performed a loader-style gate check-in (`/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U`) to bare-IP C2 server **79.124.78.197:80**, then beaconed to that same IP's **`/foots.php`** endpoint roughly every 70–90 seconds for the remainder of the capture, exfiltrating octet-stream data with a spoofed legacy-IE user agent. No delivery artifact (dropper file, hash) is present in this capture — the infection predates the recorded traffic.
